author: Atomic Shrimp
description:
Join me for a while, watching a sunset that was rendered unusually dark by a partial eclipse; the sun itself was partially obscured by cloud (as well as the moon), so this is more about the changing light and atmospheric effects than the outline of the eclipse itself.
Peak coverage (which was about 98% at this location) happens around about 44 minutes in this video.  Later at about 53 minutes it gets a bit lighter as the still partly-occluded sun - itself looking rather like a crescent moon - emerges from below the bank of cloud before setting behind the hills.
 
Slow TV isn't for everyone - nothing is scripted here - no narration or music - nothing much happens, and certainly not on purpose, but that's OK - there are no sudden loud noises in this video and no midroll ads. Mostly you will just hear the calls of birds and insects, as well as the sounds of traffic and other human activity.

This video was recorded from a hillside overlooking Santa Lucia, Cartagena, Murcia in Southeaster
title: Slow TV - Dark Sunset - Partial Eclipse in Cartagena, Murcia - August 2026
